A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework and retain matching methods and experiments. All pages, including appendices and supplementary material, were readable; figures, tables, and equations support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and reenactment experiments, ablations, qualitative results, and a user study with 30 participants in Section 4 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds comparator evaluations, inference measurements, and further ablations in Section 7.

M1.justification: The proposed framework retains the same code allocation, joint codebook learning, transformer retrieval, motion-residual compensation, appearance compensation, and optimization objective. New ablation configurations do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: VoxCeleb1 training and VoxCeleb1/CelebV-HQ evaluation remain, covering same-identity reconstruction and cross-identity reenactment. Additional qualitative examples in Figure 13 use these existing task requirements and do not establish a distinct new domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: V2 substantially broadens comparisons: LIA enters Tables 1 and 3, LivePortrait receives quantitative comparison in Table 4, and Figure 13 adds comparisons involving LIA, LivePortrait, OSFV, PECHead, and MegaPortraits. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The original training budget, 50-video sampling, reconstruction procedure, and quality metrics remain unchanged. Added supplementary protocols introduce FLOPs/FPS/memory measurements, an 82.2M-parameter control, and 256/512-code configurations. Figure 13 also uses published examples for closed-source comparisons.

E4.justification: V2 adds two substantive analyses: a parameter-matched baseline tests whether gains arise merely from model size (Table 7), and a codebook-size study tests quality and computational tradeoffs (Table 8). The earlier component ablations and code-allocation study remain; v1 Table 4 becomes v2 Table 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The user study retains the same 10 source-driving pairs, 30 participants, and preference-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in the original four tables are unchanged. V2 adds comparator, qualitative, efficiency, and ablation results. In Table 3, LIA exceeds the proposed method on FID (72.55 versus 76.47) and CSIM (0.6505 versus 0.6142), but has worse ARD (2.5404 versus 1.6234). New Table 5 reports 352.91G FLOPs and 15.13 FPS for the proposed method.

T1.justification: The codebook definitions, quantization equations, losses, and mathematical description of compensation are equivalent. Equation reformatting introduces no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about jointly learned motion and appearance codebooks, multi-scale compensation, and improved generation. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies the earlier cross-identity assessment by acknowledging LIA's appearance advantages and discussing its motion-transfer tradeoff. It adds explanations of parameter-control and codebook-size results, suggests real-time potential, and expands the retained leakage limitation with an argument that the proposed method mitigates it.

D1.justification: Core implementation and training details remain unchanged. V2 adds training-frame counts for LivePortrait and the proposed method, parameter counts and the widened-ResBlock control construction, and the RTX 3090 inference setup. Video-access instructions now direct readers to the project page.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for LIA, LivePortrait, OSFV, PECHead, and MegaPortraits, while removing DaGAN++, DreamHead, and the editable NeRF citation. The central positioning relative to motion refinement, appearance compensation, and prior codebook learning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained, with localized grammar and wording edits. Appendix A becomes separately titled supplementary material organized as Sections 6–8, additional results receive finer subsection headings, and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. Figure 1 moves to the first page, Figure 3 is rearranged, and the appearance/code-allocation diagrams exchange numbering. V2 also adds Figure 13 and Tables 4, 5, 7, and 8.

improvement.justification: The parameter-matched control and codebook-size study strengthen validation of the design, while broader comparisons and computational measurements make its tradeoffs easier to assess. V2 also acknowledges LIA's advantages and qualifies comparisons involving larger training datasets. These additions improve the evidence around an otherwise stable method, with the original experimental core and leakage limitation retained.
